summary: Shri Krishna Sharma was an Indology and linguistics scholar who taught Dieter Schuh. He founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.

Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was an Indologist. He served as Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in 1884, Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College, and permanent Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai.

Shrikant S. Bahulkar is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale. He served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and held a post at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000).

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar (1881–1967) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1914–1927), honorary secretary at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1917–1943), and General Secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference.

Shrivatsa Goswami (born 1950) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University, where he also taught. He was a visiting scholar at Harvard, was affiliated with the Vrindaban Research Institute (1994), and founded Sri Caitanya Prema Samsthana.

Shu-Fen Chen is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at National Tsing Hua University under Chin-Fa Lien and Hans Henrich Hock. Chen served as a professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

Shu-chen Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2007) under supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen Christina Lang. Chen also served as a teaching assistant there in 1996.

Shubhachandra is an Indologist who held a professorship at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and was affiliated with the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).

Shudo Ishii (born 1943) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (BA, Bungaku Hakushi) and under Shigeo Kamata. He spent his career at Komazawa University as assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor (1984, 2014), also serving at Matsugaoka Bunko.

Shuhong Chang (1904–1994) was a history, archaeology, and Sinology specialist. After studying in Lyon and Paris, he taught at Zhejiang University and the National Beiping Art Academy before serving as director and honorary director of the Dunhuang Academy from 1942 onward.

Shuichi Kato (1919–2008), a Japanology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his Dr. med. at the University of Tokyo. His appointments included professorships at the University of British Columbia (~1960–1969) and Sophia University (~1975–1985), and directorships at Ritsumeikan University.
Shuichi Maida (1906–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Haya Akegarasu from ~1927 to 1954 and studied at Kyoto University from ~1928 to 1931.

Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held positions as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (2003) and as a researcher at Bukkyo University (2003), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (2006), and Musashino University (2006).

Shujiro Shimada (1907–1994) was a scholar in Japanology, Sinology, and art history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1928 to 1931 and later held a post at Princeton University from ~1962 to 1975.

Shujun Motegi (born 1951) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned an MA at Banaras Hindu University under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi and an MA at Kyoto University, later serving as Professor of Ethics at Shinshu University.

Shuken Ito (born 1947) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral studies at Komazawa University. He held positions there as research assistant, assistant, and professor (1991), and served as visiting professor at Aichi Gakuin University (1998).

Shuman Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Northwestern University in 2014 under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn, having also studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi.

Shuming Liang (1893–1988) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Shuntian Middle School. He joined the philosophy department at Peking University in 1917 and founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and China Democratic League.

Shun Hidaka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Hidaka served as an open-call researcher at the Buddhism and Art Research Center at Otani University in 2012 and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University in 2014.

Shun'ei Hirai (born 1930) is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He served as professor (1964–2001), vice president (1986–1990), and professor emeritus (2001) at Komazawa University.
